claims: The Space Shuttle Challenger disaster occurred on January 28, 1986.
The Challenger orbiter disintegrated 73 seconds after liftoff.
The disaster killed all seven crew members.
A failed O-ring seal in the right solid rocket booster, compromised by cold temperatures, caused the fatal structural failure.
The disaster forced a 32-month shutdown of the shuttle program.
The shuttle broke up 73 seconds into flight at 11:38 a.m. EST.
The shuttle broke up 46,000 feet above the Atlantic Ocean.
A cold-induced failure of the O-ring seal allowed hot gas to breach the solid rocket booster.
The breach of the solid rocket booster led to the rupture of the external fuel tank.
The seven crew members were Dick Scobee, Michael J. Smith, Ronald McNair, Ellison Onizuka, Judy Resnik, Greg Jarvis, and Christa McAuliffe.
All seven crew members lost their lives.
Michael J. Smith was the pilot.
Dick Scobee was the Commander.
The last known words from the crew came from pilot Michael J. Smith, who said "Uh oh."
A comment from Commander Dick Scobee followed, which was cut off.
The crew cabin was found in the ocean.
The astronauts died from the massive impact (over 200 mph) of the cabin with the ocean, rather than the initial explosion.
The Rogers Commission identified the technical cause as the O-ring failure.
The Rogers Commission highlighted that NASA management ignored engineer warnings regarding the cold weather.
Christa McAuliffe was the "teacher in space."
Christa McAuliffe's lessons were performed in space in 2018.
A large segment of the Challenger was discovered on the ocean floor in 2022.
There is an upcoming limited series about the Challenger mission starring Kristen Stewart as Sally Ride, which is in development.
